metadata.title: Claude Doesn't Join Your Zoom Calls — It Builds the Bot.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude itself join a Zoom call, or does it build the software that does? Lands the carry-out that build-zoom-bot makes Claude build a meeting bot, recorder, or real-time media workflow out of Zoom's own Meeting SDK, RTMS, and a backend — it never attends a call itself.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude can personally be the Zoom bot, joining meetings itself. It can't. What it builds is the bot — the code for a meeting recorder or real-time media workflow that you run.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This skill is built from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out exactly what build-zoom-bot covers: joining meetings, recording them, or wiring up real-time media and backend services. Claude reads the file, then follows it.

beats.narration_text: For this skill, there are exactly three things it builds: a meeting bot that joins a call, a recorder that captures the session, or a real-time media workflow that processes audio and video as it happens. Each is assembled from the same three pieces — Zoom's Meeting SDK, its real-time media streams, and your own backend service. Ask it to build something outside those three and there's no mode that covers it.

beats.narration_text: Build Zoom Bot doesn't make Claude join your meetings itself — it makes Claude build the bot: a meeting bot, a recorder, or a real-time media workflow, assembled from Zoom's own Meeting SDK, RTMS, and your backend.
